# Open Source CAD and BIM Landscape

SolidCraft and FreeCAD are the two open-source tools this book uses. Bonsai is
the third reference point, because it is a native IFC authoring environment.
The category difference still matters: BIM—building information modeling—is
about building elements and their data: walls, slabs, levels, spaces, doors,
properties, and an IFC model that other tools can exchange. SolidCraft is a
parametric solid modeler for parts and small assemblies; FreeCAD spans both
Part Design and BIM.

That difference matters more than any feature table. This appendix is a
practical map, not a feature-by-feature audit. Versions move; check the current
documentation before making a decision.

## At a glance

| | SolidCraft | FreeCAD | Bonsai |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Category** | Parametric part and small-assembly CAD | General CAD with a BIM workbench | Native IFC BIM authoring |
| **IFC** | No import or export | Import/export; native IFC in the BIM workbench | Native: edits read and write IFC |
| **Building elements** | No walls, levels, spaces, or schedules | Walls, slabs, openings, levels, spaces | Walls, slabs, openings, levels, spaces |
| **Parametric history** | Sketch constraints and a feature timeline | Feature tree | BIM-parametric objects, not a mechanical feature timeline |
| **2D documentation** | Views, sections, screenshots, DXF; no drawing sheets | TechDraw sheets and annotations | Drawings generated from the IFC model |
| **Automation** | JSON commands, headless CLI, MCP | Python API | Python and IfcOpenShell |
| **Quantities** | Part-level BOM and measurements | Schedules and spreadsheets | IFC properties, schedules, quantities |
| **Collaboration** | Local files | File-based | IFC/BCF workflows; viewer and web tools |
| **Maturity** | Early (0.22.x at the time of writing) | Mature, large ecosystem | Active, mature BIM toolset |
| **License** | MIT OR Apache-2.0 | LGPL-2.1 | GPL-3.0 |
| **Best for** | Fence, deck, shed, and joinery details | One open-source tool for CAD, BIM, and drawings | OpenBIM authoring and coordination |

## What SolidCraft is good at

- **Precise parts.** Constraints, dimensions, extrude, cut, fillet, pattern,
  components, and a rebuildable timeline are the right tools for a post, rail,
  joist, or gate frame.
- **Repeatable work.** Every action is a command. The UI, CLI, scripts, and an
  AI agent use the same commands, so a simple design can be replayed and
  checked.
- **Carpentry-scale deliverables.** Figures, sections, measurements,
  interference checks, STEP/IGES export, and a part-level BOM are enough for a
  small exterior project.
- **Local ownership.** Designs are ordinary files. There is no subscription,
  cloud account, or model server.

## What SolidCraft does not do

- **No IFC.** You cannot hand a SolidCraft model to a BIM coordinator as an IFC
  model.
- **No building semantics.** There are no walls, slabs, levels, spaces, doors,
  or schedules as BIM objects.
- **No construction drawing sheets.** It renders views and sections, and can
  export a DXF view, but it is not a documentation authoring system.
- **No federated coordination.** It checks interference between bodies in one
  design; it does not coordinate architectural, structural, and MEP models.
- **No real-time multi-user collaboration.** It is a local design file.

None of that is a defect for this book. It is a boundary.

## FreeCAD in one paragraph

FreeCAD is a mature, general-purpose open-source CAD platform. Part Design
covers parametric solids; the BIM workbench adds architectural objects, native
IFC, and a path to 2D drawings through TechDraw. It also includes FEM, CAM, and
a large Python API. The trade-off is complexity: it is a platform with many
workbenches, and feature attachments can be fragile when earlier geometry
changes. Choose it when you want one open-source tool that can cover CAD, BIM,
drawings, and analysis without assembling a stack.

## Bonsai in one paragraph

Bonsai (formerly BlenderBIM) is a native IFC authoring environment built on
Blender and IfcOpenShell. It is designed for OpenBIM work: model, document, and
manage building data, with IFC as the file format rather than an export step.
Its strengths are building semantics, schedules, and coordination workflows.
The trade-off is that it is BIM-first and Blender-based; it is not a mechanical
feature-history modeler, and the learning curve is steep if you only need a
precise board or bracket.

## Using them together

A practical split:

- Model the detailed parts and small assemblies in SolidCraft.
- Export STEP, DXF, or a figure for handoff.
- If the project needs a building model, IFC coordination, or a permit set,
  assemble and document it in FreeCAD or Bonsai.

Do not expect an IFC round trip. SolidCraft has no IFC path, and a STEP export
carries geometry, not building semantics. Treat the handoff as geometry and
drawings, not as a live BIM exchange.

## Choosing for this book

For a fence, a deck, a shed, or a run of joinery, SolidCraft is the faster part
modeler: you need part precision, repeatable assemblies, and a cut list, not a
whole building model. FreeCAD is the better choice when you need TechDraw
sheets, BIM/IFC, or a single open-source platform. Part IV models the same
projects in FreeCAD so you can compare directly. Bonsai remains the specialized
native-IFC alternative.

The one-line version: **SolidCraft is an open-source parametric part modeler
that is unusually well suited to carpentry-scale work and agent-driven
workflows; FreeCAD is the broader CAD/BIM platform; Bonsai is native IFC
authoring.**
